# Promoted to repo memory: auto-update

Cite these in .sofar/repo.md by qualified handle — `auto-update M<n>` —
which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-08-05T09:43:23.576Z) — The CLI ships as THREE bundles (build.mjs): dist/cli.js is the boot entry, dist/fast.js is the hot path (boot routes only `event` and `statusline` there, speed-2 T1), dist/full.js is everything else. Two consequences that bite: (a) any code that re-launches sofar from inside sofar must spawn dist/cli.js — spawning `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` from a module bundled into fast.js runs a file with no top-level entry, which exits silently; (b) a feature added to a statusline code path lands in the fast bundle, so check `stat -f%z packages/engine/dist/fast.js` before and after. esbuild does tree-shake unused exports across the cli/ modules, so importing a heavy module for one pure helper is usually free — verify by grepping dist/fast.js for a string unique to the code you expect to be absent.
- **M2** (2026-08-05T09:43:32.260Z) — packages/engine/test/packaging.test.ts installs the real tarball into a temp prefix laid out as `<tmp>/lib/node_modules/sofar.sh/…` — a TRUE global-npm layout — and then runs the installed bin. So any product code gated on "am I a global npm install" fires for real during `npm test`: the auto-update check did a live `npm view` and wrote the developer's own ~/.local/state/sofar/update.json before it was gated. Diagnose this class of leak by deleting the suspect file, running the suite, and bisecting per test file. Fix on BOTH sides: gate the product on CI/VITEST/NODE_ENV=test, and pass the opt-out env explicitly in that test's spawn helper so the guarantee does not depend on env inheritance.
- **M3** (2026-08-05T09:47:43.093Z) — Run `sofar new <slug>` BEFORE `sofar_start_session`, never after. start_session pins the session to whatever initiative resolves at that moment, and `sofar new`'s rebinding of the branch does NOT retroactively move it — every decision, task update, memory and hook event for the rest of the session files under the OLD initiative while bindings.json innocently reads the new one. Calling sofar_start_session again with an explicit `initiative` does not fix it either: the PostToolUse hook keeps resolving through the session registry and goes on writing to the old record. Recovery that works: extract the added lines from the wrong log with `git diff -U0 <log> | grep '^+{'`, rewrite the `"initiative"` field to the right slug, `sofar import` that NDJSON (it appends and regenerates every projection), then `git restore` the wrong initiative's directory. The MCP tools' explicit `initiative` argument does route correctly, so use it for any write after the mistake is spotted.
